charges.section_title: Harboring Enemy — Foreign Personnel on Canadian Military Installations (NDA s.84)
charges.description: NDA s.84: 'Every person who knowingly harbours or conceals any person whom they know, or have reasonable grounds to believe, to be an enemy.' The CDS has authorized: (1) foreign military recruit fast-track programme (Feb 2026) despite security warnings from retired generals; (2) expanded foreign military access under NORAD, NATO, Five Eyes, bilateral, and JEF frameworks; (3) elimination of cognitive screening (CFAT) that would allow recruits to identify security threats; (4) all while CFNIS counter-intelligence is documented as compromised.
charges.max_penalty: Life imprisonment or lesser punishment (court martial)

evidence.fact: Foreign military recruit programme launched Feb 19, 2026 despite security warnings from LGen Maisonneuve and military analyst Hansen
CFAT cognitive screening eliminated Oct 2024; CFNIS counter-intelligence compromised; JEF integration expanding foreign command access

charges.legal_basis: NDA s.84 — knowingly harboring or concealing person believed to be an enemy. Opening bases to unvetted foreign personnel while senior officers publicly warn of infiltration constitutes knowing harboring.
charges.action: Court martial referral; CSIS investigation; Parliamentary inquiry
